transcript:
[00:00] Jenna: Alright everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining, I'm Jenna Morales from Redwood - AE. We have Samir (SE) with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:09] Maya: Good thanks, Maya here. Excited to see the model catalog and benchmarks.
[00:13] Tom: Tom here, CTO. We'll focus on latency and cost tradeoffs and how this plugs into our VPC/on-prem plan.
[00:20] Alicia: Alicia, security. I have a list of compliance questions but will try to keep them to the end.
[00:26] Samir: Great, I'll drive the demo and Jenna will cover next steps and pricing. Quick agenda: catalog, API/Console walkthrough, benchmarks, compatibility matrix, Q&A.
[00:36] Jenna: Quick note — this recording, we'll send links to the model catalog and a benchmark sheet after.
[00:42] Samir: Jumping in, here's the Redwood Console model catalog. You'll see curated open models and verified performance profiles. We surface latency p95, token cost, memory, and recommended quantization.
[00:52] [01:00] Samir: So if I search for 'instruction-tuned' models, you'll see rows with quick filters: latency-sensitive, cost-efficient, conversational. Each model card has a compatibility matrix that lists supported runtimes, quantizations (int8, awq, ngq), and recommended hardware like A100, H100, or NVL-2 — sorry NVL is my typo, I mean NVIDIA L4.
[01:18] Maya: Can you show the benchmark numbers side-by-side? We want to compare a few open models for a 2k token context and for embedding throughput.
[01:25] Samir: Yep, here's the comparative view. Note these are Redwood-run benchmarks on default batch sizes; we also include customer-run benchmark links. For example, Model X-13B (quant int8) shows 88ms p95 on H100 for 512 tokens and $0.0009 per token equivalent vs Model Y-70B at 140ms p95 with slightly higher cost.
[01:46] Tom: Are those numbers measured with continuous batching and KV cache on? We rely heavily on prefix caching for chat history.
[01:52] Samir: Good question. The public benchmark table indicates whether KV cache/prefix cache is enabled. These particular rows used continuous batching with KV cache enabled; we note the cache hit-rate assumptions in the footnotes. In the compatibility matrix you'll see supported caching mechanisms — some model variants require specific kernel paths to avoid OOM.
[02:13] Maya: How do we know which model will be compatible with our existing Triton/ONNX pipeline and our mixed fleet of A100s and a few on-prem A40s?
[02:20] Samir: We have a downloadable compatibility matrix CSV — it maps model architectures to recommended runtime (Torch-TRT, Triton shim, Redwood runtime), supported quant formats, and whether we recommend dedicated capacity. I'll flag a column for the A40 quirks — some older GPUs need different blocking sizes and might get slower throughput.
[02:39] Jenna: Also keep in mind Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization and batch sizing for your workload to balance cost vs latency.
[02:46] [03:00] Samir: Now demoing the API: simple REST/SDK calls. We have streaming, function calling support, and model pinning. For private deployments, the API is the same; you just point to your VPC endpoint.
[03:13] Tom: How about routing policies — can we route by latency SLO or cost tier? We might want to send low criticality requests to cheaper variants.
[03:19] Samir: Yes — smart routing policies let you set priority rules, with automatic fallback to compatible model variants in another region or to a cheaper quantized variant. You can set per-route SLOs.
[03:28] Maya: On the benchmarks spreadsheet, I saw notes about warmup and prefix caching assumptions — how sensitive are those numbers to prompt shape?
[03:34] Samir: Very. We include prompt shape buckets: short prompt (<=128 tokens), medium (129-1024), long (1k-4k). Prediction latency and throughput change with sequence length; that's why we provide per-bucket metrics. Redwood Optimize can analyze your logs (opt-in) to recommend the best model + quant profile.
[03:52] [04:00] Alicia: Security — SSO, SAML, audit logging, KMS? We need SOC2 + HIPAA controls and key management.
[04:06] Jenna: We support SSO/SAML, RBAC, per-team keys, audit logs retention options, and KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments. For hosted we have bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via supported KMS providers and enterprise HSM options — we can share the security whitepaper.
[04:23] Alicia: And is data at rest encrypted in stopgap? Any PII handling guidance?
[04:29] Jenna: Data at rest encrypted. For HIPAA use-cases we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with strict network isolation and our data retention policies can be adjusted. We'll send the SOC2 report and the HIPAA attestation.
[04:40] Tom: About dedicated capacity — we care about predictable throughput for peak hours. How do autoscale and burst work?
[04:47] Samir: Dedicated capacity is reserved GPU pools with configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. You set min/max nodes, and we provide guaranteed throughput SLAs. During heavy bursts we can spill into a burst pool if enabled.
[04:58] Maya: Pricing — do you have per-token and a flat monthly for dedicated?
[05:03] Jenna: Hosted is usage-based per-token and per-embed; Dedicated has reserved monthly commit plus usage overage. We'll send a pricing sheet tuned to your projected QPS and token volumes.
[05:12] [05:30] Samir: Back to model selection — if you have sensitive PHI, we recommend models with lower hallucination rates validated by our evals team and run in Private or Dedicated. The catalog flags models that passed Redwood-verified quality thresholds on our eval suites.
[05:43] Maya: Can you run our own accuracy evals? We have a labeled dataset of triage intents and clinical entity extraction.
[05:48] Samir: Yes, we can run benchmark jobs. For a pilot we usually: 1) run our standard throughput/latency benchmarks, 2) run accuracy tests on your labeled slice, 3) run a small production pilot on Dedicated/Private.
[06:00] Tom: How long does triage to pilot take? We have a Q4 launch window.
[06:05] Jenna: Typical pilot timelines are 2-4 weeks for a focused pilot; if you want an expanded POC with SLA evals, 6-8 weeks. Given Q4, a mid-August pilot kickoff keeps you on track.
[06:15] [06:30] Maya: About the compatibility matrix — will Samir annotate the specific tuning knobs for A40 vs A100? Our infra team prefers detailed notes.
[06:37] Samir: I'll include GPU-specific recommended kernels, block sizes, and if a quant flavor (e.g., AWQ vs GPTQ) is more stable on A40. Also note memory headroom; some 30B+ models will need model parallel or sharding.
[06:51] Alicia: Audit logs — are audit trails per-tenant and immutable? We need forensic logs for access and queries.
[06:58] Jenna: Yes, per-tenant audit logs with configurable retention. In Private deployments logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[07:06] [07:30] Samir: Quick detour — Console: you can filter models by latency/cost/quality tags, pin model versions, and run Canary rollouts with automatic fallback policies. Here's the rollout UI; you can do percent-based canaries and auto rollback if latency or error rate exceeds thresholds.
[07:48] Tom: Nice. For our use-case we need a canary that limits throughput to 5% and auto-rollback on >1% error rate. Is that supported?
[07:55] Samir: Yep. Thresholds are configurable per route.
[08:00] Maya: On Redwood Optimize — how automated is the batching/quant recommendation? Does it require sending our logs?
[08:07] Samir: There are two modes: heuristic recommendations you can run locally, and a deeper Optimize analysis that ingests anonymized logs (opt-in) to recommend batch sizes, cache TTLs, and quant profiles for cost savings. It outputs estimated token cost changes and expected latency impact.
[08:22] [08:30] Jenna: Quick objection we often hear: "we already have an in-house runtime" — many customers keep parts of the stack and use Redwood for routing and capacity.
[08:38] Tom: Yeah, our infra team has invested in Triton but we lack a good autoscaler and seamless routing across regions. Could Redwood integrate with our control plane?
[08:45] Samir: Integrations are common: we expose tracing hooks, and provide a control-plane API so you can orchestrate jobs from your existing tooling. We can also run on-prem with Private deployment so you keep the control plane.
[08:59] [09:00] Maya: Any red flags around model drift monitoring? We need regression alerts tied to eval prompts.
[09:06] Samir: Redwood has quality monitoring — you provide eval sets and we run periodic checks and alert on regressions. The Console links regressions to a prompt set and shows diffed outputs.
[09:19] Alicia: Legal/procurement question — typical contract length for Dedicated and SLAs?
[09:24] Jenna: Dedicated usually 12-36 month commits for reserved capacity with enterprise SLAs. We offer SOC2 and custom contractual terms for HIPAA customers. We can share a redlined sample.
[09:34] [09:45] Samir: Demoing a compatibility CSV download — this includes columns: model_name, arch, quant_formats, recommended_gpu, runtime_support, notes. I can pre-filter by your fleet (A100/A40).
[09:59] Maya: Please do. Also annotate the rows where customer-run benchmarks differ from Redwood-run numbers.
[10:05] Samir: We'll include both sets and the conditions (batch size, cache).
[10:12] [10:30] Tom: On fallback: if a region is congested, can we fallback to a cheaper model in another region automatically but still meet our SLOs?
[10:38] Samir: Yes, routing can prefer same-region low-latency variants and fallback to cross-region or cheaper quantized models; you declare acceptable latency thresholds per route.
[10:48] Maya: For HIPAA we might prefer Private so data never leaves our VPC. What's the typical on-prem hardware footprint?
[10:55] Samir: For a production 100 qps with 2k tokens, a small Dedicated cluster of multiple H100s or a distributed A40 pool depending on model size. For Private we'll work with your infra team to size it; sampler references included in the compatibility doc.
[11:10] [11:30] Alicia: Any surprises we should be aware of with quantization and hallucination risk?
[11:36] Samir: Quantization can slightly affect model behavior. Redwood Optimize flags quality regressions and recommends fallback profiles if accuracy dips. For critical clinical tasks we recommend higher-precision or human-in-loop checks for now.
[11:50] Maya: Can we run an accuracy sweep on the two candidate models you suggested?
[11:54] Samir: Yes — please share a slice and we'll run.
[12:00] [12:30] Jenna: Quick recap of action items and next steps — we'll send the model catalog links, benchmark spreadsheet, and security docs. Samir will share the compatibility matrix annotated for A40/A100. You (Maya) will pick 2 candidate models and a sample dataset. Alicia will consolidate compliance questions.
[12:51] Tom: Sounds good. Can we get pricing scenarios for a small pilot vs a 12-month commit?
[12:58] Jenna: Yes — I'll include hosted vs dedicated pricing and a recommended commit for target QPS.
[13:08] Maya: One more quick question — are there any known incompatibilities with our auth system (Okta)?
[13:13] Jenna: No, we support Okta via SAML SSO. Samir: I'll include setup notes for Okta provisioning.
[13:22] [13:30] Unknown: (mumble) small thing — can we integrate logs into Splunk?
[13:27] Samir: Yes, logs export to SIEM and Splunk via forwarders for Private and Dedicated.
[13:33] Alicia: Great.
[13:36] Jenna: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the pilot kickoff as discussed.
[13:42] Maya: Thanks, bye.
[13:44] Tom: Bye.
[13:45] Samir: Thanks all.
[13:47] Jenna: End.
